mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the FEDFUNDS rate predicts higher discount rates for future cash flows, reducing the present value of expected equity returns and thus producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during periods of rising FEDFUNDS (p > 0.05), or the discount rate sensitivity to FEDFUNDS is estimated below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by falling unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the next 3 months
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, SPX forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS is rising and UNRATE is falling (p > 0.05), or the interaction coefficient is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in industrial production (INDPRO) above the prior quarter's average is interpreted as growing economic demand, which elevates equity risk premia and yields negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: More than 40% of INDPRO monthly jumps above prior quarter median are followed by non-negative 5-day SPX forward returns (p < 0.05), or the effect is not statistically robust.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months suggests supply-side easing, lowering growth expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative in >70% of CPIAUCSL < 2% periods (p > 0.05), or the inflation coefficient is positive and significant.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25 percentage points in a single month, it signals persistent tightening, which raises real interest rates and dampens equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative during such FEDFUNDS moves (p > 0.05), or the effect size is negligible.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% triggers a labor market tightening that increases investor confidence, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% in a month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE crosses below 4% (p > 0.05), or the effect is not robust across regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in retail sales proxy (not available in the given catalog; fallback to HOUST as a demand proxy) above trend predicts higher corporate earnings expectations, yielding positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: More than 60% of HOUST monthly increases above trend are not followed by positive 5-day SPX returns (p > 0.05), or the coefficient is not significant.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months indicates weakening demand, which reduces growth prospects and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative in >50% of INDPRO decline periods (p > 0.05), or the effect is not statistically significant.
